newsitem.title: UK: Bank of Scotland seen higher on H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Scotland seen higher on H1 results.

text.p: Shares in Bank of Scotland Plc are seen higher on Wednesday after the group posted a better-than- expected 24 percent rise in first-half pre-tax profit, traders said.
"The figures were certainly above the top end of the range and will be received very well," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage.
Bank of Scotland said profits rose to 324.3 million stg from 261.6 million stg a year before, compared with expectations mostly in a range between 283 million stg and 305 million.

Stripping out the effects of last year's one-off 23.6 million stg gain from the sale of the bank's 50 percent stake in Halifax Credit Card, and this year's inclusion of Bank of Western Australia, the underlying rise was also 24 percent.
The dividend was raised to 2.91p from 2.45p, also at the top end of the range of forecasts between 2.2p and 3.0p.

The stock was up 8-1/2p at 264 by 0712 GMT and other banks were also firm with Royal Bank of Scotland Plc up 8p at 508-1/2, National Westminster Bank Plc up 2p at 694 and Lloyds TSB Group Plc up 2p at 385-1/2.

In a statement, Bank of Scotland said the results were achieved against generally benign economic conditions in the UK and U.S., and there were "no signs of any change in direction in the present, broadly favourable banking climate."
